question: Compare the nutritional composition of egg whites, whole milk, and heavy whipping cream on a standardized 100g basis.
golden_sql: SELECT i.common_name, np.serving_basis, np.calories_kcal, np.protein_g, np.fat_total_g, np.carbohydrates_g, np.water_g FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.nutritional_profiles np ON i.ingredient_id = np.ingredient_id WHERE np.is_100g_normalized = TRUE AND i.ingredient_id IN ('ING_EGG_WHITE', 'ING_WHOLE_MILK', 'ING_HEAVY_CREAM') ORDER BY np.protein_g DESC;
semantic_distinctions: Must NOT compare 1 cup of cream to 1 egg white. Comparing by volumetric portion introduces severe mass and density artifacts.
expected_explanation_elements: Egg white is a concentrated protein-in-water solution (~88% water, ~11% protein, virtually zero lipid).
Heavy cream is a high-fat oil-in-water emulsion (~36% fat, ~2% protein, ~58% water).
Whole milk is a balanced emulsion (~88% water, ~3.3% protein, ~3.3% fat).

question: What molecular properties make egg whites uniquely suited for rapid foam formation and overrun?
golden_sql: SELECT c.compound_name, c.molecular_weight_kda, c.isoelectric_point_pi, c.denaturation_temp_c, c.functional_role, fp.quantitative_value AS overrun_percent FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.functional_properties fp ON i.ingredient_id = fp.ingredient_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.chemical_compounds c ON fp.compound_id = c.compound_id WHERE i.ingredient_id = 'ING_EGG_WHITE' AND fp.property_category = 'Foam Formation' ORDER BY c.molecular_weight_kda ASC;

ground_truth_criteria.rapid_adsorption_agent: Ovotransferrin and globulins (lower molecular weight, surface flexible)

semantic_distinctions: Distinguish foaming capacity (overrun/volume, driven by fast diffusion of smaller globular proteins) from foam stability (drainage resistance, driven by ovomucin viscosity and interfacial crosslinking).
expected_explanation_elements: Globular proteins unfold at the air-water interface during shear.
Hydrophobic groups orient toward the air phase; hydrophilic groups orient toward the water phase.
Forms a continuous viscoelastic cohesive interfacial film preventing bubble coalescence.

question: Explain the difference in stabilization mechanisms between fat-stabilized foam (whipped cream) and protein-stabilized foam (meringue).
golden_sql: SELECT i.common_name, m.mechanism_name, m.mechanism_class, m.primary_stabilizing_agent, m.structural_outcome, m.temperature_sensitivity, mr.relationship_type, mr.impact_summary FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.mechanism_relationships mr JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i ON mr.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m ON mr.mechanism_id = m.mechanism_id WHERE i.ingredient_id IN ('ING_EGG_WHITE', 'ING_HEAVY_CREAM') ORDER BY i.ingredient_id;

ground_truth_criteria.meringue_mechanism: Interfacial protein denaturation and cohesive viscoelastic film formation
ground_truth_criteria.cream_mechanism: Partial coalescence of solid fat globules forming a 3D structural skeleton around bubbles
ground_truth_criteria.temperature_dependence_cream: Requires chilled temperatures (4-8°C) so fat remains partially crystalline
ground_truth_criteria.temperature_dependence_egg: Can be whipped at room temperature (20°C); thermal baking sets the protein gel

semantic_distinctions: In cream, fat IS the structural stabilizer. In egg white foam, free fat is an interfacial DESTABILIZER that destroys bubbles.
expected_explanation_elements: Cream requires crystalline fat platelets to pierce adjoining globule membranes during whipping, creating a rigid network.
Meringue relies on unfolded ovalbumin, lysozyme, and ovomucin creating surface elasticity without any fat skeleton.

question: Why does free lipid or egg yolk contaminate and collapse egg white foam, while fat is essential to whipped cream?
golden_sql: SELECT i.common_name, m.mechanism_name, mr.relationship_type, mr.impact_summary, m.description FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.mechanism_relationships mr JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m ON mr.mechanism_id = m.mechanism_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i ON mr.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE mr.relationship_type = 'DESTABILIZES' OR m.mechanism_id = 'MECH_LIPID_INTERFERENCE_PROTEIN_FOAM';

ground_truth_criteria.lipid_action_on_protein: Spreads over air-water interface faster than proteins, displacing viscoelastic protein films without providing mechanical cohesion
ground_truth_criteria.result_in_egg_foam: Premature lamella rupture and bubble collapse
ground_truth_criteria.contrast_with_cream: In cream, lipids are contained in discrete globular membranes that partially coalesce into a protective matrix at low temperatures

semantic_distinctions: Free lipid spreading vs discrete membrane-bound fat globule aggregation.
expected_explanation_elements: Triglycerides have low surface tension and high mobility.
Displaced protein films lose dilatational elasticity.
Even 0.1% yolk lipid reduces egg white overrun by more than 70%.

question: What mechanisms and hydrocolloid stabilizers prevent foam drainage, and what is their empirical drainage half-life?
golden_sql: SELECT i.common_name, i.category, fp.property_name, fp.quantitative_value AS drainage_half_life_min, fp.unit_of_measure, fp.test_conditions, m.mechanism_name, m.structural_outcome FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.functional_properties fp ON i.ingredient_id = fp.ingredient_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.mechanism_relationships mr ON i.ingredient_id = mr.ingredient_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m ON mr.mechanism_id = m.mechanism_id WHERE fp.property_category = 'Foam Stability' AND m.mechanism_id = 'MECH_DRAINAGE_RETARDATION_VISCOSITY' ORDER BY fp.quantitative_value DESC;

ground_truth_criteria.viscosity_mechanism: Steric hindrance and high zero-shear viscosity retarding liquid drainage through Plateau borders (Stokes' Law)

semantic_distinctions: Distinguish thermodynamic bubble stabilization (preventing coalescence) from kinetic drainage retardation (slowing gravity syneresis via continuous-phase viscosity).
expected_explanation_elements: Stokes' law dictates drainage velocity is inversely proportional to liquid viscosity.
Xanthan gum forms an entangled polymer mesh in the aqueous lamellae.
Prevents thinning of liquid films between air bubbles.

question: What happens nutritionally and structurally if egg white is replaced with skim milk and xanthan gum in an aerated dessert?
golden_sql: WITH baseline AS (SELECT i.ingredient_id, i.common_name, np.protein_g, np.fat_total_g, np.carbohydrates_g, np.calories_kcal, MAX(CASE WHEN fp.property_category = 'Foam Formation' THEN fp.quantitative_value END) AS overrun_pct, MAX(CASE WHEN fp.property_category = 'Foam Stability' THEN fp.quantitative_value END) AS drainage_t_half FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.nutritional_profiles np ON i.ingredient_id = np.ingredient_id AND np.is_100g_normalized = TRUE LEFT JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.functional_properties fp ON i.ingredient_id = fp.ingredient_id WHERE i.ingredient_id IN ('ING_EGG_WHITE', 'ING_SKIM_MILK', 'ING_XANTHAN_GUM') GROUP BY i.ingredient_id, i.common_name, np.protein_g, np.fat_total_g, np.carbohydrates_g, np.calories_kcal) SELECT 'Egg White' AS system, protein_g, fat_total_g, carbohydrates_g, calories_kcal, overrun_pct, drainage_t_half FROM baseline WHERE ingredient_id = 'ING_EGG_WHITE' UNION ALL SELECT 'Skim Milk (99.5%) + Xanthan (0.5%)' AS system, ROUND((m.protein_g * 0.995) + (x.protein_g * 0.005), 2), ROUND((m.fat_total_g * 0.995) + (x.fat_total_g * 0.005), 2), ROUND((m.carbohydrates_g * 0.995) + (x.carbohydrates_g * 0.005), 2), ROUND((m.calories_kcal * 0.995) + (x.calories_kcal * 0.005), 1), ROUND(m.overrun_pct * 0.65, 1), ROUND(x.drainage_t_half * 1.15, 1) FROM (SELECT * FROM baseline WHERE ingredient_id = 'ING_SKIM_MILK') m CROSS JOIN (SELECT * FROM baseline WHERE ingredient_id = 'ING_XANTHAN_GUM') x;

ground_truth_criteria.nutritional_shift: Protein drops from ~10.9g to ~3.4g per 100g (~68% reduction); carbohydrates rise due to lactose in milk (~5g/100g); calories drop slightly or remain comparable (~50 kcal vs ~37 kcal)
ground_truth_criteria.structural_shift: Overrun is significantly lower (skim milk + xanthan reaches ~250-400% vs 800% for egg white); drainage stability is maintained or improved via xanthan viscosity; heat-setting ability is lost (cannot bake into rigid meringue)

semantic_distinctions: A substitution may match room-temperature stability (drainage) without matching baking coagulability (thermal denaturation).
expected_explanation_elements: Milk proteins (casein micelles) lack the rapid surface expansion of ovalbumin.
Xanthan gum compensates for drainage by thickening water, but cannot form covalent disulfide bridges upon heating.

question: Which ingredients contain proteins with measured foam overrun exceeding 400%?
golden_sql: SELECT i.common_name, c.compound_name AS active_protein, fp.property_name, fp.quantitative_value AS overrun_percent, fp.unit_of_measure, fp.test_conditions FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.functional_properties fp ON i.ingredient_id = fp.ingredient_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.chemical_compounds c ON fp.compound_id = c.compound_id WHERE fp.property_category = 'Foam Formation' AND fp.quantitative_value >= 400.0 ORDER BY fp.quantitative_value DESC;
semantic_distinctions: Differentiate foaming overrun (volume increase during aeration) from emulsion capacity or gel firmness.
expected_explanation_elements: High overrun requires high surface hydrophobicity and conformational flexibility to rapidly reduce interfacial tension at the newly created air boundary.

question: Trace the mechanism of interfacial protein denaturation back to its supporting peer-reviewed scientific publications and DOIs.
golden_sql: SELECT m.mechanism_name, m.mechanism_class, se.title, se.authors, se.journal_or_book, se.publication_year, se.doi_or_url, se.study_methodology, se.key_findings, se.evidence_confidence FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.scientific_evidence se ON m.mechanism_id = se.mechanism_id WHERE m.mechanism_id = 'MECH_PROTEIN_DENATURATION_INTERFACE' ORDER BY se.publication_year DESC;

ground_truth_criteria.key_citation_author: Foegeding, E. A. or Dickinson, E. or Belitz, H.-D.
ground_truth_criteria.publication_venue: Food Hydrocolloids or Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry or Food Chemistry
ground_truth_criteria.methodology: Interfacial dilatational rheology and drop shape tensiometry

semantic_distinctions: Citing peer-reviewed journal papers versus general culinary rules of thumb.
expected_explanation_elements: Studies quantify the elastic storage modulus of the protein layer at the air-water boundary.
Confirms irreversible mechanical unfolding during shearing.

question: What peer-reviewed evidence demonstrates that partial coalescence of fat globules stabilizes dairy foams?
golden_sql: SELECT m.mechanism_name, se.title, se.authors, se.journal_or_book, se.publication_year, se.doi_or_url, se.key_findings, se.study_methodology FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.scientific_evidence se ON m.mechanism_id = se.mechanism_id WHERE m.mechanism_id = 'MECH_FAT_PARTIAL_COALESCENCE';

ground_truth_criteria.cited_researchers: Walstra, P. or Goff, H. D. or Fredrick, E.
ground_truth_criteria.key_finding: Solid fat crystal platelets protruding from milk fat globules pierce neighboring membranes, forming an interconnected network at low temperatures (4-8°C)

semantic_distinctions: Complete coalescence produces bulk butter/liquid oil (catastrophic foam collapse); partial coalescence creates a rigid structural scaffolding.
expected_explanation_elements: Temperature must remain below triglyceride melting points (~15-20°C).
Partial coalescence provides high yield stress and stiffness to whipped cream.

question: How does cooking temperature affect the structural properties of egg white proteins, and at what temperatures do ovalbumin and ovotransferrin denature?
golden_sql: SELECT compound_id, compound_name, compound_class, molecular_weight_kda, denaturation_temp_c, functional_role FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.chemical_compounds WHERE compound_id IN ('CMP_OVALBUMIN', 'CMP_OVOTRANSFERRIN', 'CMP_OVOMUCIN') ORDER BY denaturation_temp_c ASC;

ground_truth_criteria.functional_significance: Ovotransferrin coagulates first, initiating foam setting; ovalbumin provides final rigid crumb structure during baking at >80°C

semantic_distinctions: Ovalbumin is resistant to thermal denaturation at room temp and requires baking heat to fully crosslink, whereas mechanical shear unfolds it at the air interface.
expected_explanation_elements: Thermal denaturation exposes free sulfhydryl (-SH) groups that form covalent disulfide (-S-S-) crosslinks.
Transforms a transient wet foam into a solid porous meringue matrix.

question: Compare the recipe-level macronutrient density and calories per 100g of classic meringue against traditional whipped cream.
golden_sql: SELECT r.recipe_name, ROUND(SUM(ri.quantity_g), 1) AS batch_mass_g, ROUND((SUM(ri.quantity_g * (np.calories_kcal / 100.0)) / SUM(ri.quantity_g)) * 100, 1) AS calories_per_100g, ROUND((SUM(ri.quantity_g * (np.protein_g / 100.0)) / SUM(ri.quantity_g)) * 100, 2) AS protein_per_100g, ROUND((SUM(ri.quantity_g * (np.fat_total_g / 100.0)) / SUM(ri.quantity_g)) * 100, 2) AS fat_per_100g, ROUND((SUM(ri.quantity_g * (np.carbohydrates_g / 100.0)) / SUM(ri.quantity_g)) * 100, 2) AS carbs_per_100g FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.recipes r JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.recipe_ingredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.nutritional_profiles np ON ri.ingredient_id = np.ingredient_id AND np.is_100g_normalized = TRUE WHERE r.recipe_id IN ('RCP_CLASSIC_MERINGUE', 'RCP_WHIPPED_CREAM_TOPPING') GROUP BY r.recipe_id, r.recipe_name ORDER BY calories_per_100g DESC;

ground_truth_criteria.meringue_calories_per_100g: 200 - 240 kcal/100g (dominated by sucrose carbs ~50%, fat ~0.1%, protein ~4-5%)
ground_truth_criteria.fat_difference: Whipped cream is >30g fat/100g; meringue has <0.2g fat/100g

semantic_distinctions: Meringue is virtually fat-free but carb-dense due to added sucrose; whipped cream is fat-dense with minimal carbohydrate.
expected_explanation_elements: Formulation macros reflect the physical stabilization agents: lipid network vs sugar-stabilized protein lamellae.

question: Which food science mechanisms or interactions in our database have limited evidence or are classified as untested hypotheses?
golden_sql: SELECT m.mechanism_id, m.mechanism_name, m.evidence_confidence, COUNT(se.evidence_id) AS citations_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN mr.is_hypothesized = TRUE THEN 1 END) AS hypotheses_count, CASE WHEN COUNT(se.evidence_id) = 0 THEN 'NO_EVIDENCE' WHEN COUNT(se.evidence_id) < 2 THEN 'LIMITED_EVIDENCE' ELSE 'ROBUST' END AS evidence_status FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m LEFT JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.scientific_evidence se ON m.mechanism_id = se.mechanism_id LEFT JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.mechanism_relationships mr ON m.mechanism_id = mr.mechanism_id GROUP BY m.mechanism_id, m.mechanism_name, m.evidence_confidence HAVING COUNT(se.evidence_id) < 2 OR COUNT(CASE WHEN mr.is_hypothesized = TRUE THEN 1 END) > 0;

ground_truth_criteria.identified_gaps: Highlights novel hydrocolloid synergy hypotheses or poorly documented culinary folk mechanisms (e.g. copper bowl ion stabilization nuances vs modern pasteurized whites)
ground_truth_criteria.adherence_to_rules: Complies with Data Rules 5, 7, and 8: distinguishing hypothesis from established finding

semantic_distinctions: Do not treat absence of evidence as evidence of absence; recommend specific experimental assays needed.
expected_explanation_elements: Clarify what experimental data would be necessary to substantiate the hypothesis.

question: How does whipping temperature impact the drainage half-life and success rate of heavy cream foams in experimental trials?
golden_sql: SELECT e.experiment_name, pm.process_name, pm.temperature_range_c, e.overrun_percent, e.drainage_half_life_min, e.bubble_size_mean_um, e.is_successful, e.conclusion FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_experiments e JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.processing_methods pm ON e.process_id = pm.process_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.ingredients i ON e.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id WHERE i.ingredient_id = 'ING_HEAVY_CREAM' ORDER BY pm.temperature_range_c ASC;

ground_truth_criteria.chilled_condition (4-8C): Successful: Overrun ~110%, high drainage stability (t1/2 > 240 min), small uniform bubbles (~18-25 um)
ground_truth_criteria.warm_condition (>20C): Failed: Catastrophic churn/phase separation into butter or thin runny emulsion, low overrun, rapid collapse

semantic_distinctions: Liquid fat destroys foaming; semi-solid crystalline fat stabilizes foaming.
expected_explanation_elements: At 4°C, solid fat content of milk fat is ~40-50%, optimal for partial coalescence.
At 22°C, solid fat content drops below 15%, causing complete coalescence or spreading.

question: Why does adding sugar early during egg white whipping delay foam expansion, while adding it late preserves overrun?
golden_sql: SELECT m.mechanism_name, m.structural_outcome, mr.impact_summary, c.compound_name, se.key_findings FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_mechanisms m JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.mechanism_relationships mr ON m.mechanism_id = mr.mechanism_id JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.chemical_compounds c ON mr.compound_id = c.compound_id LEFT JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.scientific_evidence se ON m.mechanism_id = se.mechanism_id WHERE c.compound_id = 'CMP_SUCROSE';

ground_truth_criteria.early_addition_effect: Sucrose binds water, increases bulk viscosity, and stabilizes native protein conformations, drastically slowing the rate of protein unfolding at the air interface; requires longer whipping time and lowers final overrun
ground_truth_criteria.late_addition_effect: Added after initial foam network forms; sugar dissolves into lamellae, increases continuous-phase viscosity, prevents water evaporation, and stabilizes the formed foam against syneresis

semantic_distinctions: Sucrose is an overrun inhibitor during initial aeration, but a stability enhancer in the mature foam.
expected_explanation_elements: Timing of sucrose addition represents a kinetic trade-off between expansion rate and foam stability.

question: What is the measured overrun and stability of egg white foams across varying whipping durations?
golden_sql: SELECT e.experiment_id, e.experiment_name, pm.duration_seconds, e.overrun_percent, e.drainage_half_life_min, e.bubble_size_mean_um, e.sensory_texture_score, e.conclusion FROM workspace.foodmechanics_silver.food_experiments e JOIN workspace.foodmechanics_silver.processing_methods pm ON e.process_id = pm.process_id WHERE e.ingredient_id = 'ING_EGG_WHITE' ORDER BY pm.duration_seconds ASC;

ground_truth_criteria.underwhipped: Low overrun, large loose bubbles, poor drainage half-life
ground_truth_criteria.optimal (soft/stiff peaks): Max overrun (~800-900%), small uniform bubble diameter, high elasticity
ground_truth_criteria.overwhipped: Coagulation into clumps, syneresis/graininess, bubble rupture due to protein over-aggregation

semantic_distinctions: Excessive mechanical shear causes excessive protein insolubilization and clumping (grainy texture).
expected_explanation_elements: Optimal whipping balances interfacial area with cohesive lamellar strength.

question: Query the Gold analytical view v_mechanism_evidence to list all documented mechanisms and their peer-reviewed literature citations.
golden_sql: SELECT mechanism_name, mechanism_class, active_compound, ingredient_name, relationship_type, paper_title, authors, journal_name, publication_year, doi FROM workspace.foodmechanics_gold.v_mechanism_evidence ORDER BY mechanism_name, publication_year DESC;
semantic_distinctions: Demonstrates use of curated Gold analytical views for direct Genie agent consumption.
expected_explanation_elements: Provides rapid end-to-end provenance traceability from culinary outcome to peer-reviewed science.
